reviews.title: Can’t use unless you pay.
reviews.text: You can’t save your photos without paying for a monthly subscription. You can screenshot them, but it leaves your edited photo with an egregious watermark. You don’t find this out until you’ve completed what you’re working on and then try to export it. Time wasted that didn’t have to be, if the devolpers weren’t so deceptive.

reviews.title: Used to enjoy, now the ads are ridiculous
reviews.text:
I enjoy trying new game apps. I understand that’s what I signed up for on the free version.
I don’t at all enjoy getting hung up in the app and not being able to download my collage to my phone.  That feels incompetent.
Also not a fan of you refusing to let me leave a review from the app, when I select that I’m not enjoying it in the pop up you make me answer. That feels skeezy.
Incompetent + Skeezy on the same visit = hard pass on the paid version

Pro Tip: if you want someone to consider paying for your product, give them an excellent, annoyance-free experience on the free portion. 

Load it down with ads, just make the experience glitch and skeez free.

reviews.title: Insane pricing for pro features

It’s the pop-up that asks us if we love using Pic Stitch. I’m using an iPad Pro 12.9 inch. And I am unable to click anything once that pops up. It’s very annoying.

reviews.title: $200 a month? Uninstalled
reviews.text: It’s one thing for an app developer to put all of the features behind a paywall. That’s a choice, and of course I’ll be moving to something with free basic features. But what’s particularly disgusting about these developers is that they try to make their $35 a year for a collage app look like a good deal by some outrageous $200 a month pricing scheme to anchor people. It’s so disingenuous, dishonest and manipulative. I almost never review apps but went out of my way for this one.
